chunks: Tamim ibn Abdullah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Ali Al-Ansari, on the authority of Abi Salt al-Harawi, who said:

I was with Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) when a group of people from Qum entered and greeted him. The Imam greeted them back and paid his respects to them. Then Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) told them, ‘You are welcome. You are truly our followers. There will come a time when you will visit my shrine in Toos. Indeed, whoever visits me having already performed the ritual bathing (‘Ghusl) will be purified from all his sins just as the day he was born from his mother.’

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (a title of Imam Ali ibn Musa)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the shrine of Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (a.s.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith highlights the spiritual elevation of the people of Qum as early adherents who received the Imam's personal welcome. It establishes the theological principle that visiting the shrine in Toos serves as a means of *kaffarah* (expiation), cleansing the believer of sins to the state of *fitrah* (innocence) akin to the day of birth, a concept deeply rooted in Shia devotional practice.
